title: Finite Q3 cutoff scaling of the raw commutator-sum Trotter coefficient
question: When the registered finite Q3 oscillator cutoff is varied at fixed volume and source fixture, how does the raw operator-norm commutator coefficient entering the Lie-Trotter bound scale, and does this finite audit provide a cutoff-independent coefficient?
method: Follow the EXP-001162 manifest chain to the hash-pinned finite Q3 physical fixture and reconstruct truncated oscillator matrices for cutoffs 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 on volumes 2, 4, and 6.

Compute every local onsite and bond norm and the exact overlapping-support commutator sum C_V(n), with disjoint supports set to zero and one full tensor embedding checked at the declared reference cutoff.
Evaluate the fixed-step unitary coefficient h^2 C_V(n)/(2N) and the corresponding unit-norm history coefficient without substituting a cutoff-independent constant.
Rebuild the calculation in an independent lane, compare all volume/cutoff rows and diagnostics, and compile Lean R333 for exact rational coefficient bookkeeping.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 61/61 assertions over 15 volume/cutoff rows; the integrated verifier passes 219/219 with Lean R333 PASS. At every declared volume the raw commutator sum is zero at the two-level truncation, becomes positive at cutoff 3, and is monotone on the finite grid: C_2 grows from 1.6175067619642274 at n=3 to 20.051691329669865 at n=6 (ratio 12.396666153852731), C_4 from 6.4700270478569095 to 80.20676531867952, and C_6 from 11.322547333749593 to 140.36183930768902. The associated fixed N=12 unitary coefficients grow to 0.09283190430402714, 0.37132761721610885, and 0.6498233301281898, while q norm grows by 3.324257433552119 and the maximum local term norm by 19.594303361153024 across n=2 to 6.
decision_reason: The finite audit establishes a reproducible cutoff-scaling table for the exact bounded-matrix coefficient used by EXP-001162. The monotone finite-grid growth, together with the zero two-level commutator caused by the severe truncation, shows that the raw coefficient cannot be carried forward as an unqualified cutoff-independent numerical constant. This is a route-local diagnostic only: it is not an asymptotic divergence theorem and does not decide whether an energy/state-weighted or quadratic-form coefficient can be made uniform.
boundary: Finite oscillator cutoffs 2 through 6, volumes 2, 4, and 6, inherited compact-source fixture, fixed horizon 1/3 and N=12 coefficient only. No infinite-cutoff theorem, common unbounded core, direct D/delta-D Cauchy estimate, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A, or Clay conclusion.
next_action: Replace the raw operator-norm coefficient only with a separately proved energy/state-weighted or quadratic-form estimate on a named common core; test source, beta, volume, and cutoff uniformity before attempting any common-alpha or QFT reconstruction step.
open: common unbounded operator domain and core density
source/beta/volume-uniform direct D and delta-D Cauchy
gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: Both lanes reconstruct q, p, onsite, bond, and commutator matrices for every declared cutoff; no n=3 row is reused.
Union-support commutators agree with a full tensor embedding at V=2,n=3 within the declared tolerance; disjoint pairs are exactly zero by tensor structure.
All reported coefficients are raw bounded operator norms; no weighted or quadratic-form estimate is smuggled into the result.
The ratio and monotonicity fields are labelled finite-grid diagnostics; the zero n=2 row is retained and no infinite-cutoff lower bound is asserted.
Only the inherited source fixture and three finite graph volumes are covered; source, beta, volume, exhaustion, and common-alpha uniformity remain open.
The result records a QFT-facing route boundary and does not close a common core, thermodynamic dynamics, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, or Pre-A.
Lean R333 checks exact rational bookkeeping only; numerical matrix norms and all analytic promotion gates remain outside Lean and explicitly open.

qft_interface.closed: A reproducible finite-cutoff table and independent/Lean cross-check establish the behavior of the raw bounded-matrix Trotter coefficient on the inherited Q3 fixture.
qft_interface.open: A cutoff-independent raw coefficient, energy/state-weighted replacement, common domain, thermodynamic history, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 evidence only; no TECT production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

no_overclaim: This finite cutoff-scaling audit records a route-local boundary for the raw operator-norm Trotter coefficient. It does not prove asymptotic divergence or uniformity, and it does not prove any QFT, C6, Sector A, Pre-A, or Clay result.
